standard_text: 8.6A describe the volume formula V = Bh of a cylinder in terms of its base area and its height; 8.6B model the relationship between the volume of a cylinder and a cone having both congruent bases and heights and connect that relationship to the formulas; 8.7A solve problems involving the volume of cylinders, cones, and spheres
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 volume worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.6A, 8.6B and 8.7A: volume of cylinders, cones and spheres, in terms of π and with 3.14, and real-world problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Cylinder πr²h, cone ⅓πr²h, sphere ⁴⁄₃πr³.
key_sub: A cone is one third of the cylinder with the same base and height.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Cylinder: V = Bh = πr²h, where B is the area of the circle base.
  • Cone: V = ⅓πr²h. A cone holds one third of a cylinder with the same base and height.
  • Sphere: V = ⁴⁄₃πr³.
  • Use the radius, not the diameter.

Examples

Example

Cylinder r = 3, h = 10

π × 9 × 10

Answer: 90π

Example

Cone r = 3, h = 10

⅓ × 90π

Answer: 30π

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using the diameter as the radiusr = d ÷ 2.
Forgetting the ⅓ for a coneA cone is one third of the cylinder.
Squaring instead of cubing for a sphereV = ⁴⁄₃πr³ uses r³.

items.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 2 m and height 5 m. Use π ≈ 3.14.

A cylinder has volume 100π in³ and height 4 in. What is its radius?
items.e: 100π = π × r² × 4, so r² = 25 and r = 5 in.

items.q: Find the volume of a sphere with radius 3 m. Use π ≈ 3.14.
A sphere has volume 36π cm³. What is its radius?
items.e: ⁴⁄₃πr³ = 36π, so r³ = 27 and r = 3 cm.

items.q: Find the volume of a cylinder with radius 5 m and height 4 m. Use π ≈ 3.14.
A cone has volume 12π cm³ and radius 3 cm. What is its height?
items.e: 12π = ⅓ × π × 9 × h = 3πh, so h = 4 cm.

items.q: Find the volume of a cone with radius 6 m and height 5 m. Use π ≈ 3.14.
A cone has volume 50π m³ and height 6 m. What is its radius?
items.e: 50π = ⅓ × π × r² × 6 = 2πr², so r² = 25 and r = 5 m.
